answer.rationale: p99 latency on the write path is elevated but the constraint (security patch cannot revert) and settlement peak conditions rule out rollback. memory_b5 shows read replica routing successfully reduced dashboard load on the primary without affecting transactional write latency recovery. Routing eligible read queries away from primary frees write capacity during peak settlement traffic. This preserves the security patch, avoids the cost of regional failover or circuit breaking (which risk customer impact), and aligns with proven mechanism. Verification confirms read replica routing does not degrade write path performance.
